image_description: Two white, box-shaped studio monitor speakers positioned side-by-side on a white background. The left speaker shows a large central driver (woofer) and two smaller circular components below it, along with control knobs. The right speaker shows only the large central driver. There is text/logos at the top center of the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both objects clearly exhibit a rectangular, box-like geometry typical of bookshelf speakers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left speaker has one large cone and two smaller circular elements; the right has one large cone. They are circular and on the front face.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While there is a large woofer, the secondary elements on the left speaker are positioned *below* the woofer, not above or beside in a typical vertical stack. The right speaker lacks a visible tweeter entirely. This deviates from the 'typical' description provided in the checkpoint.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers show a dark central cone and a lighter grey surround, consistent with rubber or foam surrounds found on real speakers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers are exposed; no grille cloth is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows only the front and partial side views; the rear panel is completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosures appear to be painted white, likely MDF or plastic, matching the description.
The object is functionally identifiable as a speaker system.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The logos and text at the top are nonsensical and malformed, characteristic of AI-generated text artifacts. They do not form legible words.

The two small black circles below the main woofer on the left speaker lack clear definition. They appear to merge slightly into the white casing without distinct bezels or functional logic (e.g., are they ports? knobs? drivers?). Their placement and rendering look physically ambiguous compared to standard speaker designs.
The perspective lines of the right speaker's box seem slightly inconsistent with the left speaker, and the depth perception of the side panel feels flattened.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker (studio monitor vs generic) and validate class alignment.
To verify the 3D consistency of the boxes and ensure the drivers are properly recessed/protruding rather than floating textures.
To check if the circular drivers have clean boundaries against the enclosure and if the 'knobs' on the left speaker are distinct entities.
To analyze the gibberish text at the top and confirm it is an artifact rather than a stylized logo.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and any subtle texture anomalies in the white casing.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the text/logos at the top.
Physical plausibility and boundary clarity of the two small circular elements on the left speaker.
Geometric consistency of the speaker enclosures (parallel lines, corner sharpness).
Texture realism of the speaker cones and surrounds.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the two small black circles on the bottom of the left speaker. Do they look like functional audio components (ports/knobs) or AI hallucinations? Also, evaluate the severity of the text artifacts at the top—are they distracting enough to significantly lower the quality score?
